title: Not me going to see a play with @go see a play!  . . #theatre #spooky...
transcript: telling spooky ghost stories in an Irish pub on a dark windy night the Weir is a revival of a 1997 play by Conor McPherson which I've been curious to see for years so when I heard that Irish Rep was bringing it back I jumped at the opportunity to see it and ultimately it didn't disappoint I will say it took me a while to get into the play it starts off kind of slow the mood is kind of quiet and naturalistic with a lot of casual chatter between the characters about this and that and I had a little bit of a mentality of like “get to the ghost stories already!” but by the end I really appreciated how it lets us settle into the setting and get to know the characters and that the stories themselves wouldn't mean much to us by the end without the context by the end we find that the play is exploring some deeper questions about what purpose ghost stories actually serve both on a communal and personal level and what happens when it crosses that line from from the communal to the personal? and likewise what does it mean to feel haunted by something both literally and emotionally? this is a play that requires some patience from the audience but for me I found that it paid off in an extremely satisfying way fun fact for my UK followers they're actually about to do this play in the West End starring Brendan Gleeson and actually directed by Conor Mcpherson himself and I liked the play enough that if I were in London this fall I'd honestly go see it again but for those of us in New York this Irish Rep revival is running right now through August 31st and hot tip if you're under the age of 40 you can actually get $25 seats
